questions.q: Whom did Saul take with him to seek David in the wilderness of Ziph?
questions.a: Saul took three thousand chosen men of Israel.

questions.q: How did David know that Saul was coming after him into the wilderness?
questions.a: David sent out spies and learned for certain that Saul had come.

questions.q: Where did David go after learning that Saul had come?
questions.a: David arose and went to the place where Saul had camped.

questions.q: What did Abishai want to do when he and David saw Saul sleeping inside the camp?
questions.a: Abishai wanted to strike Saul with his own spear and pin him to the earth.

questions.q: Why did David not want Abishai to kill Saul?
questions.a: David said no one could kill Yahweh’s appointed king and be innocent. He said that Yahweh will surely punish anyone who kills him.

questions.q: How did David say Saul must die?
questions.a: David said that Yahweh may cause him to die, or he may die of some disease or of old age, or enemy soldiers may kill him in a battle, but David would not kill him.

questions.q: What did David take from beside Saul’s head?
questions.a: David took the spear and the jug of water from near Saul’s head.

questions.q: Where did David go after he left Saul’s camp?
questions.a: He went across a valley and stood on the top of the hill far away from Saul’s camp.

questions.q: Why did David say Abner, the man who was to watch over Saul, deserved to die?
questions.a: He said Abner deserved to die because he did not watch over his master, the anointed of Yahweh.

questions.q: What question did David ask Saul?
questions.a: David asked why his master was pursuing David, his servant, and what evil he had done.

questions.q: What did David say should happen to the people who had caused Saul to be angry with him?
questions.a: David said that they should be cursed before Yahweh because they had driven him out from the inheritance of Yahweh.

questions.q: What did Saul say to David?
questions.a: Saul said that he had sinned, had acted foolishly, and would not harm David anymore. He asked David to come back home.

questions.q: What did David tell Saul to do about his spear?
questions.a: He told Saul to send one of his young men over to get it.

questions.q: What did David say about the value of both of their lives?
questions.a: David said that just as Saul’s life was great in his eyes that day, he hoped that Yahweh could consider his own life to be great and rescue him from every danger.

commentary.text: Saul goes after David, who again spares Saul's life.

Verses 1–12 How soon do unholy hearts lose the good impressions convictions have made upon them! How helpless were Saul and all his men! All as though disarmed and chained, yet nothing is done to them; they are only asleep. How easily can God weaken the strongest, befool the wisest, and baffle the most watchful! David still resolved to wait till God thought fit to avenge him on Saul. He will by no means force his way to the promised crown by any wrong methods. The temptation was very strong; but if he yielded, he would sin against God, therefore he resisted the temptation, and trusted God with the event.

David reasoned seriously and affectionately with Saul. Those who forbid our attendance on God's ordinances, do what they can to estrange us from God, and to make us heathens. We are to reckon that which exposes us to sin the greatest injury that can be done us. If the Lord stirred thee up against me, either in displeasure to me, taking this way to punish me for my sins against him, or in displeasure to thee, if it be the effect of that evil spirit from the Lord which troubles thee; let Him accept an offering from us both. Let us join in seeking peace, and to be reconciled with God by sacrifice.

Saul repeated his good words and good wishes. But he showed no evidence of true repentance towards God. David and Saul parted to meet no more. No reconciliation among men is firm, which is not founded in an cemented by peace with God through Jesus Christ. In sinning against God, men play the fool, and err exceedingly. Many obtain a passing view of these truths, who hate and close their eyes against the light. Fair professions do not entitle those to confidence who have long sinned against the light, yet the confessions of obstinate sinners may satisfy us that we are in the right way, and encourage us to persevere, expecting our recompence from the Lord alone.
